newsitem.title: USA: General Acceptance has losses, sets restructuring.
newsitem.headline: General Acceptance has losses, sets restructuring.

text.p: General Acceptance Corp., reporting losses for the fourth quarter and full year, said Tuesday it reached a new agreement with Conseco Inc., its primary lender.
Under terms of the agreement, Conseco will give it a $70 million revolving line of credit and in return will get the right to stock and control of one-third of the board of directors.
The agreement expires Jan. 1, 1998, and concludes a nearly 15-month period during which the company operated under default to Conseco, General Acceptance said.
General Acceptance is a specialised consumer finance company that purchases and services instalment contracts for purchasers of used automobiles.
For the quarter, General Acceptance had a loss of $7.4 million, or $1.23 a share, compared with a loss a year earlier of $3.1 million, or 51 cents a share.

For the year, it lost $9.08 million, or $1.51 a share, compared with a profit of $717,000, or 13 cents a share. Revenues, which were reported only for the year, rose to $30.97 million, compared with $25.64 million a year earlier.
The company said the new agreement gives it sufficient lines of credit to fund acquisitions and other business ventures throughout 1997.
The company said it closed financing operations in several areas and its plans to concentrate the majority of its resources on Indiana, Ohio and Florida.

As part of its refinancing, the company said it issued notes to Conseco Inc. and certain major stockholders that, under certain circumstances, may be convertible into common stock. If Conseco and the others converted their notes, Conseco would own about 32 percent of the total common stock.
General Acceptance stock was unchanged at $3.25 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
